The President: I don't know that that's exactly what I'm saying.
Alex, you understand what I'm saying? What do you understand?

Alex: Thank you Sir for this opportunity. Sir, it suggests that even if they wanted to be healed yesterday, the healing wouldn't have taken place yesterday, they couldn't have been healed. This is the moment for the healing.

The President: Yes. So this is the moment for the healing. It's about the timing for the healing, and that is a problem. It's inconsistent with our Gospel, cause the truth of the matter is that he's not trying to heal you now. He's not working on it. He did it a long time ago. Right?

I want to show you something in the Bible. I want you to notice what the word says.
Chante, if you're listening, I'm sure that God is giving you a song. If you've been listening.

James 5:14-15

Vs.15 - The prayer of faith shall save the sick. That means heal him, restore him... right? Look at the Lord's responsibility in this...."and the Lord shall raise him up." Doesn't say the Lord shall heal him.
What's the Lord's role? The Lord's role is the strength that he gives him.
The Greek word sozo means deliver/save/restore, as is translated. So the prayer of faith, meaning it's our words, the words we speak in faith. The prayer of faith shall save the sick. So this guy was going to die, but the prayer of faith saved him/delivered him/restored him. It's not about God's answer, it's the words of faith. If you say, "Be healed," you're not praying to God.

Acts 3, where Peter and John met that man who was impotent in his feet, never walked from birth. Remember? What did Peter say to him? "Such as I have, give I you." He didn't pray to God to release his power. He said "What I have, I give you." That's amazing. "I give you." "Such as I have, I give you." That's amazing! That's not like praying to the Father to give him. Then he goes "In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth..." that's a demand! Peter demanded that he rise up and walk! "He, leaping up, stood." That's where God's response comes in. He gives the man power/strength, because Peter demanded it. So the power of the Lord is present to make it happen. Remember, it says "His feet and ankle bones received strength, and he, leaping up, stood." His feet and ankle bones "received" strength. "The lord is the strength of my life." So, strength is present. Power is present.
Do you get it? So you see that it's not about when it's God's timing to heal. It's about when you're ready to receive healing that was given a long time ago.

The most beautiful part... cause I look at the songs and I think that somehow, in a general sense, it's okay, but it still needs to rise in understanding. I say that because I don't think that our picture of the Lord is good enough. I'll explain that to you.
When I say Jesus is my saviour, he's not saving me now. He saved me. So we call him saviour, not because he's in the work of saving now. He's already accomplished his work of salvation. He's not into the activity of saving, but it's one of his titles. We say "Our saviour, Jesus Christ, " not because he's doing it now. As saviour, we're saying he saved man, he saved the world. He's called saviour of the world.
Now when we come to healing and say he's the great physician, it's not because he's doing it now. He's not practicing any surgery right now. He's not healing you now. He's the great physician because it's part of his titles. Like he's the great God. The great creator. He's not creating right now. He's the creator because he created. The Bible says he created all things, so he's the great creator. He's the ruler, he's not ruling everything.

So when we mix that reality and bring it to a kind of nebulous atmosphere, there seems to be a little bit of confusion. Like we don't really know what we're saying when we say that he's healing you now. We need to start moving to the phase of the actual truth of the Gospel. Right? We need to, so that the language of our communication doesn't confuse us.

Look at what he said, after sending them out. He said "heal the sick." You, heal the sick, because he gave them both power and authority to heal all manner of sickness and diseases among the people, in his name. Same power and authority we have. In fact, what's remarkable is that the authority they had is not even comparable to the authority we have. You may ask what the difference is. Oh, tremendous difference! Christ before the cross and Christ after the cross, significant difference in his authority. Today is not the day for that discussion, but if you listen to our messages about the mystery of Christ, the mystery of the Church, the life of the saints, you'll learn a lot from what I just told you.

So, "he's always on time," no. He's not the one they're waiting for. That's why people say "God's time is the best." Like he fixed a time. But it's not true.
So you're going to change that line, right?

Dcn. Raph: Pastor, thank you Sir. From what you just told us now, we have a different understanding now. Much clearer than what we've known. I'm also looking at the people in the healing line, after being taught from the healing school, it's at the time Pastor comes out that they get healed.

Dcn. Raph: So there is timing, but we're taking it wrongly that it's God we're expecting. Thank you, Sir.

The President: Yeah. Yeah.

Pst. Saki: Pastor good evening, Sir. I wanted to ask, what then is the difference when you talk about the chronos and the cairos, the timing of God, and the timing of men, like you've just explained?

The President: Beautiful! If you've listened to a lot of what I've shared in the last few years, I was pointing the people to God's timeline. My point was, where are we in God's timeline? Now, if we know God's timeline, we know how to synchronize ourselves, by his grace and power, with his timing for the world. God has a plan, and I am in the world at this moment in God's timing. There are certain things that are divine that you have no influence on.
For example, you didn't choose your parents. You couldn't have. You didn't choose your siblings. You couldn't have. So you can't change those ones. You can't change the things that were not your plan. You didn't choose the day you were born. But you're here now, so why were you born? Why did you come to this family? All of that is God's working.
Now, do I by that mean every human being in this world was brought in on a divine purpose? I don't mean that at all, because the Bible doesn't even say so. There's a biological law that's been established as to how people come into this world. So we cannot say that everyone that's born into this world was born on God's plan. How then do we know those who were born on God's plan? Very simple!

There are 3 groups in the world.
1. Those who were born according to God's plan: they're located within the Gospel of Jesus Christ. He gave us his message with which to find them. They cannot believe in him, except they were chosen to believe in him. Jesus said, "No man can come to me, except the Father draws him. When we preach the Gospel, we locate men and women according to the divine predestination.

2. Vessels of wrath: they were also chosen by God as to when and how they would come into this world, and they would be used to further the work of God. But they're not children of salvation. They will not be saved. They will be destroyed. They're used for the furtherance of God's words.
Simple example in the Bible: Pharaoh, compared to Moses and the children of Israel. The Bible says God chose Pharaoh and raised him for this purpose. And when you study the scriptures, you'll find that there are more than that. That's why he used the term "vessels of wrath." These people were chosen for destruction.

3. This 3rd group came simply by biological generation. They were not planned for by the will of God, but by the will of man. Because of that, they will be extinguished.
For example, in the Old Testament, when God said to the children of Israel "I will not give you the land all at once, but gradually...lest the beast of the field multiply against you." Cause if they got all the land, they were going to have trouble. The animals would multiply against them. So he would do it step by step, so that there would be balance in the ecosystem.
We go after the ones we want, and don't care about how the ecosystem works. Then we get ourselves into trouble, eating the ones we can, driving the ones we think we have power over, but leaving the powerful ones that we're afraid of. And if that's too much for us, we run away. We know there are pythons/tigers/leopards in that place, and want to run away. So he said he would do it gradually. He would have their population increase so they could occupy the land.
Now man also, in his will, produces children. That helps also, because population is good. What's the advantage of the Nigerian population? It's good for the economy. Work force. How many rich people are carrying things at the motor parks? None of them, but there's a lot of labour there. How many are carrying cement on their heads? None of them. But the cement's got to be moved. Somebody's got to do them. That's why when you discover the word of God, the message you hear is important. Don't let those people out there deceive you about what you hear. They don't understand anything. This word that you hear, the message that you receive determines the quality of your life. Always remember that.

So in scripture, he let's you know:
There are those who were born of the will of God.
There are those who were born of the will of man.
There are those who were born, just pure biology.
Can I show it to you from the Bible?

John 1:12-13

No matter the story they tell you, it was God's plan for you to come. Then you thank God, because he has a full plan for your life.
Then of course, the others he planned for, they can't believe. They're appointed to wrath.
So timing is very important to God. It's based on his plan.

Alright, so Tyoumi 's going to do something about a couple of lines there, right?

So when we say "Your healing has come," the only reason their healing has come is because we have come. We appointed the date. We appointed the timing. We said to them, "Get ready! These 3 days, this and this and this is going to happen." Why? "Because we were sent to you, and we chose a convenient time to do this." So we say, "Get ready, you will be healed!" And they will be! Yeah.

*Tuesday, 30th June 2026*

*- The word "abide" to be changed.*

Nice song!
But I'm just thinking through one line there, and wondering why he chose to use that word. Why did you choose to use the word "abide?"
The program, I believe you're singing to them with regard to faith in that moment, for that occasion, on that day. "Abide" is long-term. If you're singing it in Church for general exhortation, that would be the word. But if you want to use it for a program like this, it can't be the word "abide."
And then you said "Only believe." That already tells us you're addressing that particular congregation for them to receive salvation or healing or whatever they desire of the Lord.
This is not church now, because church is full of believers. So "Let your faith in him abide" is already a contradiction.

So, can we change the word "abide?"

*Dcn. Taiwo:* Thank you, Sir.
What about "arise?"

*The President:* Well, the word "believe" and the word "faith" are the same. One is a noun, and one is a verb. You're saying "Let your faith in him arise," from where? Is the faith sleeping?
It's like a message coming to you, and as it's coming to you, faith cometh by hearing. So it's assumed that there was no faith until you hear the word we're bringing to you. You said, "As we bring the word of life to you," so as we bring the word, faith comes.

So I don't know if "arise" will be the best word there, because we're bringing the word, and faith's coming. That's why we're saying "Only believe," that means "Act now on your faith that's coming to you from the word."

*Dcn. Taiwo:* We can look for a better word, Sir. We can change the line.

*The President:* Okay. You could also change the line so that you don't turn it into a conundrum there.

Okay, so we'll wait for you to fix that.
Thank you!

*Sunday, 19th July 2026*

*THE INSTRUCTION*
*- "The Lord already made you whole" in the bridge was changed to "You will be healed in Jesus name."*
*- "Devils" to be replaced with "demons" in the chorus.*

*THE DIALOGUE THAT LED TO INSTRUCTION*
Thank you very much!

Just a couple of things.
The first one, I didn't really like the way you pronounced the "centurion." In your singing, it sounded like a completely different word. Because of the way you said0g, it can be assumed that it's a completely different word.

Then, in the pre-chorus, I would rather use the word "demons" for "devils." You've got it in two lines there in the chorus. So, replace the word "devils" with "demons" in the chorus.
And by the way, in the verse, you noticed you already used the word "demons" already. So that just goes with what I was saying.

The other one. I've got a bit of a question. It opens the bridge by saying, "The Lord already made you whole." If the Lord already made you whole, why is the moment coming? Cause it says, "The moment is here for your miracle," and then "The Lord already made you whole."
It says, "We declare to you that you'll be healed." So why the inconsistency?

*Pst. Sylvia:* Thank you, Sir. That line where we have "You'll be healed," what I had there before was "We declare to you his finished works." So when I changed that, it didn't seem correct.

*The President:* Yeah. It's a healing program, so it's incorrect. What I would rather change here is "The Lord already made you whole." It challenges everything else you're saying.

*Pst. Sylvia:* Alright, Sir. I'll change that, Sir. I'll put it in the present continuous like what we have in the song.

*The President:* Let me explain something to you. And it will help you in considering your lyrical content.
It is true that Jesus Christ completed everything for salvation. So legally, all the world is saved. Right? Because God's not holding their sins against them, for the very fact that Jesus paid the full penalty for sin. But then, why did Peter tell the whole house of Israel that they shall be saved if they believed in Jesus? Why did Paul tell the jailer, "Believe in the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shall be Saved?" And in Romans 10:9 "If you will confess with your mouth the Lord Jesus, and shall believe that God raised him from the dead, thou shall be saved?" But they're all saved, legally. But they haven't entered into vital salvation.
So, wholeness is a completely different thing, except that the word "saved" is an all-inclusive word which, on one hand, is beautiful because it includes everything. On the other hand, it makes your analysis of salvation a little bit more clumsy, except you know the details of the scripture. So that's why it can be like a contradiction for some, while it is perfectly in order.
So when you're dealing with sinners, you have to have a consistency in your delivery.
For example, every sinner is saved legally. But not a one of those sinners is righteous before God. Can you see it? Because to be righteous, you must believe in Jesus Christ. You must believe. You must believe in his resurrection. You must believe. You must. If you don't believe, you cannot have his righteousness. But that righteousness was consummated in Christ 2,000 years ago, and legally made available to all men. But you cannot be righteous until you believe.
Do you get it?
Yeah. So that's the same thing as being made whole. The wholeness, you will not enter until you believe. And that's what your song is saying here. "Just say 'Yes, I believe it.'"
And that's why I said it can become clumsy when we mix them up.
Like in the Healing Streams, we say "God will heal you," because God is doing it anyway. And I've explained before, it's not like God is doing some work about it. We're bringing them healing through the Gospel of Jesus. What he already did in Christ. The salvation that we are now covers everything. But we have to be consistent in the presentation.
"Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shall be saved." That's God's word.
So, we separate the legal from the vital.

So that's the line I think you should change. The one in the bridge.

*Pst. Sylvia:* Pastor Sir, what about "You will be healed In Jesus name?"

*The President:* Yeah.

*Pst. Sylvia:* Thank you, Sir.

Thank you!

comments.text:
*Monday, 18th May 2026*
 
 *INTSTRUCTION*
*- Soloist to be placed on overdrive with more complex songs, so as to leave the monotony of his singing.*

*THE DIALOGUE THAT LED TO THE INSTRUCTION*
So, this song is done as simple as possible, not to get in trouble.
So, what class is this song? I think we have about 4-5 classes of songs. When I say classes, I'm talking about ratings.
We have about 5 classes. Where do you rate this one?

Let's say we have some songs that have been SONG OF THE YEAR, WORSHIP SONG OF THE YEAR, HIT SONG OF THE YEAR... yeah. Then you have the BEST SONGS.
So, if we pick from BEST SONGS up to SONG OF THE YEAR, we have 5 categories, right? So where do you think this one comes in? Do you see this song being listed as BEST SONG? Would you give this song such an award?

*Sammie:* Yes, Sir.

*The President:* Why? Which part of it gets your attention? The verses, or the coda?

*Sammie:* The verse.

*The President:* Which of the verses? Tell me, so that I'll read it to you.

*Sammie:* Verse 1.

*The President:* Okay. Here's what it says. "You're the Word from the start/Full of glory and grace/Life and light to every man/Hope for all the human race/In You all things consist/You uphold the world by the power of your word/Your word is greater than all/Lord of all."
That part turns you on?

*Sammie:* And the chorus too.

*The President:* Then, the chorus. "Lord Jesus, you are/The beginning and the end/Faithful and true/None compares to you/Source of truth/The everlasting God/King of the earth/All power is yours."
Wow! Wonderful!
(The President sings) "Source of truth/The everlasting God/King of the earth/All power is yours." Right? Did I get that part?

*Sammie:* Very well, Sir.

*The President:* I got it? How could I? Okay. So, it's very simple.
You really want us to sing this song in the coming Praise Service?

*Sammie:* I would love to, Sir.

*The President:* I don't mean whether you would love to. I mean, you want us to sing it?

*Sammie:* Whatever you want us to do, Sir.

*The President:* What I want us to do? I didn't invite you before you brought it up here.
And I noticed you were also trying to stay away from the previous way. You just made it softer.

So, I want us to put you through some more complex songs. Get him to sing some more complex songs, just to free him from the monotony. I mean, he's a good singer, no doubt. We need to get him to do some other songs.

There are some of you, I notice when you sing other songs in church, and you sing well. But when you come here, it's like you're restricted to some particular songs.

I think we should put Sammie on overdrive. He would love it!

*Ogey:* Pastor Sir, if you would permit me, I wanted to suggest HEAVENLY FATHER by Pst. Saki.

*The President:* I agree. I mean, he will try it. Yeah. Why not?
Thank you. Good one!

*Evang:* Pastor, good evening, Sir. I don't know if it's the same issue that's happening with Sis. Rozey.
Pastor, you once gave an experiment many years ago. You said you put an insect in a bottle and capped it. The insect jumped and jumped, trying to come out, but couldn't. When the cap was removed, it still couldn't get up there, because it had been conditioned.
Now, surely, the issue that Sis. Rozey had, and which several other people also had... When the great exchange happened, it was like she was going to faint, so we had to do something. But Dcn. Isaiah and Dcn. Kelly were not in agreement.

Pastor Sir, I'm saying this so that you can help us. The fear of failing, the fear not being accepted, and the fear of not getting that standard that you've set for us, if these can be taken care of, Rozey can become the best singer on earth.

This is what we've been dealing with actually. It was to save a soul. So I told her to remain there, and when Pastor asks, I will explain. This is really the issue. If Rozey would do a thousand rehearsals and not take care of this, it's a problem.
If Sammie is having that kind of mind also, there's an issue.
Pastor Sir, you've given us wings to fly. Sir, if you can help us, this great exchange will work for her, and bring out the best results.

*The President:* (Smiles) So Rozey, you were crying because I said you should move from Soprano to Alto? I told you yesterday that that was not a demotion. It's the flesh. Imagine if you think you're a great singer, and you're put in a place where those people are not as good, then there's a mistake.

I think recently, probably in the last few weeks, probably Michaela has done more songs than most, except Maya maybe. Where's she singing from? Alto.
Think how many songs Rita has done. Or Eniola. They've done more songs than most people on this side (Soprano). So don't feel bad about those things. And when I tell you to do something, even if you don't understand it at that time, know that it's for your best interests. Look at it from both sides, for ministry and for you as a person. If it's good for the ministry but not good for you, I'm not going to do it. If it's good for you but not good for the ministry, I'm not going to do it. I always like to ensure that it's good for both.

It's the same thing like when we want to transfer a pastor. I want to make sure that pastor should be in that place. If you make someone do something that God does not sanction, you'll bear responsibility. It's a displacement, because you're helping someone to stay outside of God's work. It doesn't matter whether he succeeds or fails. That's not important. What's important is, is he in the centre of God's will? Why would you make someone do something that God does not accept? Why would you help a man/woman to get out of God's will? Who wants to bear such a responsibility? At least not me.

In the last couple of days before you came here, Friday into Saturday, I was speaking to a studio audience of the Global Ministers' Classroom. One of the things I said to them was that I like to see what I'm going to do before I do it. And that's the way I've done most things, cause I believe very much in visions. Not dreams. I don't take dreams seriously. I believe in visions. So I like to know what a person should do before I encourage a person to do it. I don't like guess work. And I haven't misled a single person yet.
So, what you just need is some confidence. The Praise Night that we are doing, do we say Praise Night with Rozey? No. With Pastor Chris. So if that same Pastor Chris is saying "sit on this side," be happy. Don't feel bad. We love you very much! Don't feel bad. At least I do. Yes! Don't be sad.

So, always have confidence, alright? The direction that we give is always in your interest. Always. We may talk to a few of you more than others, but it doesn't mean that they are priced more than you. But we have to talk with a few that help give inspiration/help/direction to others. I may not meet with everybody here individually. But at least, with a few, it sends a message.
I think it was some weeks ago when we were here, I asked if some people knew the song. The ones who didn't, I said 500 Espees each. Where are they? Did you get it? Oh, but you didn't acknowledge. You were going to do that today? Where have you been all this while? How much is 500 Espees? Almost a million Naira. How can someone give you almost a million Naira and you don't even acknowledge that they did? No, no, no, no, I'm not saying that they're not grateful. They are very grateful, I can see that. And I've not been here, really. But that's the point. Even though they're grateful they received a gift, they don't even have the chance to walk their way to meet me.
Okay, Eli-J wants to see me, he goes to stop me when I'm getting into the vehicle. You get it? So he gets to see me. That doesn't mean that I don't love those ones there, but some people do get an opportunity ahead of others. Right?

Thank you!

So, I've received your acknowledgement from your standing (500 Espees beneficiaries). I'm glad you got it.

*Saturday, 18th July 2026*

 
*THE INSTRUCTION*
*- "The glory of my existence" was changed to "My glorious and loving Father."*
*- Sing title was also changed from THE GLORY OF MY EXISTENCE to MY GLORIOUS AND LOVING FATHER.*

*THE DIALOGUE THAT LED TO THE INSTRUCTION*
What's the meaning of the line, which is also the title, "The glory of my existence?" What does it mean?

*Vashaun:* Thank you very much, Pastor Sir.
What first comes to my mind is the very essence of my being.

*The President:* "The glory of my existence" is the first line of the chorus. What does it mean?
Rita, what's the meaning of "The glory of my existence?"

*Ritasoul:* Sir, what I understand...

*The President:* What you understand? But you've been singing it all this while.

*Ritasoul:* Sir, he's the glory of my life. He lives in me. He's the glory of my entire being.

*The President:* I'm trying to understand it. Does anybody understand it? Well, you've all been singing it, so I suppose you know what you've been singing. So, can you tell me what's the meaning of that first line? Rozey and Chookar?

*Chookar:* Good evening, Pastor Sir. Thank you for the opportunity, Sir.
I'm thinking it means the essence of my being, the reason I'm living, my purpose for being in existence.

*The President:* The essence of my being? Yeah, but it says "The glory of my existence." How are they related?
Eniola?

*Eniola:* Pastor, thank you Sir. I think they're saying the beauty of my life in the person of the Holyspirit. Because the other song that we have says "The glory of your presence is the glamour of my life." So, I think the writer is just trying to be flowery to describe the beauty of the person of the Holyspirit.

*The President:* I can see that they're talking about the Holyspirit with many other words. But my questio is, what is the meaning of "The glory of my existence?" Are you saying that the word "existence" is synonymous with the word "life?" I'm asking a simple question with respect to the terminology that's given to us in that first line. I'm trying to get the thinking. What is the glory of my existence?
Okay, Kresthill.

*Kresthill:* Thank you, Sir. What I think that line means is the quality of my being. The beauty of my being. Just like the scripture says that we are not sufficient of ourselves, but the Lord is our sufficiency. In line with that scripture, I can understand that line to be that the Spirit of God is the quality of my existence.

*The President:* What is existence?

*Kresthill:* Existence is being.

*The President:* What do you mean by being?

*Kresthill:* The idea of existence comes from awareness.

*The President:* So, like a mad man who isn't aware that he exists?

*Kresthill:* I think a mad man is aware that he exists.

*The President:* Not all of them. That's why we say they're mad. They're not conscious of their reality.

*Kasid:* Thank you very much, Sir. I think whatever the writer was trying to explain, from my understanding, is encapsulating the daily life of a man, his day to day living, his relationships, the expression of his daily life. Pastor, you told us that we can't live without the Holyspirit. He's bringing his relationship with the Holyspirit and his daily life together. I think that's what he meant by "The glory of my existence."

*The President:* I think that maybe some of you are not understanding my question. I understand that they're relating it to the Holyspirit. I know that the whole song is about the Holyspirit. It's obvious. My question is about the construction, "The glory of my existence."

Let me give you an example of what I'm looking at here, as I try to unravel the choice of words.
I can say "I can see everything with my eyes," and I can say "I can see everything with my opticals." Do you get it? When I say "eyes," it's simple for you to understand. But when I use "opticals," You don't know the totality of my consideration. A I talking about my eyes, or my eye glasses? There are other opticals... my binoculars. What might i be considering with that construction?
When you say "The glory of my life," it's easy. But when you say "existence..." it's a much bigger word. This "exist" is not a being. A being has a self. So when you say "The glory of my existence, " I'm wondering, as a thing that exists, or??? I'm asking, why that choice in the first place?
Is there a reason for the choice? Maybe you do, that's what i'm trying to understand. You may be right, you may be wrong.

*Uche:* Thank you very much, Sir. Why I would think that he used that word "existence" would be not as in human life, but as in our oneness in Christ by the Holyspirit. It's a new life. Like one of our songs you corrected, where we said "created us in Christ," and you told us it would be better constructed "recreated," because everything was created. It's like generalizing. So this new life, it comes by the Spirit of God. I think that's what was intended. It's like one of our songs that says "Your very life and nature you imparted to our Spirit is the reality of our oneness with you." What makes that real is the Spirit of God.

*The President:* You are still centering your discussion on the Spirit and us. There's no question there. I'm in total agreement. The whole song already expresses that. That is real. That is clear.
I just question the choice of words.

*Dcn. A4:* Thank you, Sir. Good evening, Sir.
What I had in mind was not just about life. I was thinking about daily functionality. Everything I do. The reason for my being.

*The President:* I thought, how could you escape "life," with everything you're saying?
There's a difference between "The reason for my existence" and "The glory of my existence." When you say "The reason for my existence," you're dealing with a completely different thing from "The glory of my existence."
I'm asking about "The glory of my existence." I want to know what it means.

*Dcn. A4:* Sir, you have now opened my eyes to what I was saying. I know what i want to say, but I'm not using the right words. I'll wait to hear from you what it does mean.

*The President:* (Smiles) Now he's put the responsibility on me to explain what he thought. So that's like asking Joseph to interpret your dream. Or Daniel to interpret your dream. That's very interesting.

*EXHORTATION*
You know, words are very important. How we construct what we say, especially if you're going to put it in a song that could be sung always by so many, it needs to be clear. It's very easy to assume. Anybody can assume what it means, but what does it really mean?
So why do we say "The Holyspirit is the beauty of my life?" If there's no beauty in your life, you can't claim it. It's just like some sinners, when you're preaching to them, who say "God is in all of us." It's not true. Some have Satan in them. And Jesus said it, "You are of your father, the devil. And the works of your Father, you will do." So we can't allow them to rub that on us.

Does something have glory because it exists? Satan exists. Does he have any glory? The reason you can say that the Holyspirit is the glory of your life is not because he's the glory of all life, because not all who live have glory. Some live unto themselves. There's no glory.
So, when I questioned it, I wanted to know what you meant. Do you mean that there's glory because you exist?
Before you were born again, you existed. When we talk about our life in Christ, it's a new life, not a new existence. When you're born again, you have a new life, "as if" you never existed before. "As if" because all things become new. But your body is the same, it doesn't become 2 months old like a baby's. No. It's spiritual. There's an existence. You become a new creature, as if you never existed before. You have a completely new life. But there is a history, so you became born again. The reason there is "again" is because there was a body.
We can't confuse the words of Jesus and say when you're born again, you never existed before. No. You're a new person. In the spirit, you are a new person. You have a new life that never existed before.

Now, when you sing, it's like the bridge transedes into another part of the song. Right now, it's not leading anywhere. But from the bridge, replace the chorus with what you have as the coda, which becomes the refrain.
So take the coda twice, go back to the pre-chorus, take the coda again twice because it's now a refrain. Then the third time in it, you end it with "Your word is limitless, " the way it is currently.

So, from the bridge, to pre-chorus, which you sang as a solo, even though I would like to hear it with everyone. To the refrain twice, then back to pre-chorus, to refrain twice. The third time, it ends with your new coda, "Your word is limitless."
So, you may want to take the prechorus the second time as "all." But let's hear it.

Now, go from "Align with your imperial command," to the pre-chorus. Now I want everybody to sing the pre-chorus. From there into the refrain.

*Saturday, 18th July 2026*

 
*THE INSTRUCTION*
*- "The glory of my existence" was changed to "My glorious and loving Father."*
*- Sing title was also changed from THE GLORY OF MY EXISTENCE to MY GLORIOUS AND LOVING FATHER.*

*THE DIALOGUE THAT LED TO THE INSTRUCTION*
What's the meaning of the line, which is also the title, "The glory of my existence?" What does it mean?

*Vashaun:* Thank you very much, Pastor Sir.
What first comes to my mind is the very essence of my being.

*The President:* "The glory of my existence" is the first line of the chorus. What does it mean?
Rita, what's the meaning of "The glory of my existence?"

*Ritasoul:* Sir, what I understand...

*The President:* What you understand? But you've been singing it all this while.

*Ritasoul:* Sir, he's the glory of my life. He lives in me. He's the glory of my entire being.

*The President:* I'm trying to understand it. Does anybody understand it? Well, you've all been singing it, so I suppose you know what you've been singing. So, can you tell me what's the meaning of that first line? Rozey and Chookar?

*Chookar:* Good evening, Pastor Sir. Thank you for the opportunity, Sir.
I'm thinking it means the essence of my being, the reason I'm living, my purpose for being in existence.

*The President:* The essence of my being? Yeah, but it says "The glory of my existence." How are they related?
Eniola?

*Eniola:* Pastor, thank you Sir. I think they're saying the beauty of my life in the person of the Holyspirit. Because the other song that we have says "The glory of your presence is the glamour of my life." So, I think the writer is just trying to be flowery to describe the beauty of the person of the Holyspirit.

*The President:* I can see that they're talking about the Holyspirit with many other words. But my questio is, what is the meaning of "The glory of my existence?" Are you saying that the word "existence" is synonymous with the word "life?" I'm asking a simple question with respect to the terminology that's given to us in that first line. I'm trying to get the thinking. What is the glory of my existence?
Okay, Kresthill.

*Kresthill:* Thank you, Sir. What I think that line means is the quality of my being. The beauty of my being. Just like the scripture says that we are not sufficient of ourselves, but the Lord is our sufficiency. In line with that scripture, I can understand that line to be that the Spirit of God is the quality of my existence.

*The President:* What is existence?

*Kresthill:* Existence is being.

*The President:* What do you mean by being?

*Kresthill:* The idea of existence comes from awareness.

*The President:* So, like a mad man who isn't aware that he exists?

*Kresthill:* I think a mad man is aware that he exists.

*The President:* Not all of them. That's why we say they're mad. They're not conscious of their reality.

*Kasid:* Thank you very much, Sir. I think whatever the writer was trying to explain, from my understanding, is encapsulating the daily life of a man, his day to day living, his relationships, the expression of his daily life. Pastor, you told us that we can't live without the Holyspirit. He's bringing his relationship with the Holyspirit and his daily life together. I think that's what he meant by "The glory of my existence."

*The President:* I think that maybe some of you are not understanding my question. I understand that they're relating it to the Holyspirit. I know that the whole song is about the Holyspirit. It's obvious. My question is about the construction, "The glory of my existence."

Let me give you an example of what I'm looking at here, as I try to unravel the choice of words.
I can say "I can see everything with my eyes," and I can say "I can see everything with my opticals." Do you get it? When I say "eyes," it's simple for you to understand. But when I use "opticals," You don't know the totality of my consideration. A I talking about my eyes, or my eye glasses? There are other opticals... my binoculars. What might i be considering with that construction?
When you say "The glory of my life," it's easy. But when you say "existence..." it's a much bigger word. This "exist" is not a being. A being has a self. So when you say "The glory of my existence, " I'm wondering, as a thing that exists, or??? I'm asking, why that choice in the first place?
Is there a reason for the choice? Maybe you do, that's what i'm trying to understand. You may be right, you may be wrong.

*Uche:* Thank you very much, Sir. Why I would think that he used that word "existence" would be not as in human life, but as in our oneness in Christ by the Holyspirit. It's a new life. Like one of our songs you corrected, where we said "created us in Christ," and you told us it would be better constructed "recreated," because everything was created. It's like generalizing. So this new life, it comes by the Spirit of God. I think that's what was intended. It's like one of our songs that says "Your very life and nature you imparted to our Spirit is the reality of our oneness with you." What makes that real is the Spirit of God.

*The President:* You are still centering your discussion on the Spirit and us. There's no question there. I'm in total agreement. The whole song already expresses that. That is real. That is clear.
I just question the choice of words.

*Dcn. A4:* Thank you, Sir. Good evening, Sir.
What I had in mind was not just about life. I was thinking about daily functionality. Everything I do. The reason for my being.

*The President:* I thought, how could you escape "life," with everything you're saying?
There's a difference between "The reason for my existence" and "The glory of my existence." When you say "The reason for my existence," you're dealing with a completely different thing from "The glory of my existence."
I'm asking about "The glory of my existence." I want to know what it means.

*Dcn. A4:* Sir, you have now opened my eyes to what I was saying. I know what i want to say, but I'm not using the right words. I'll wait to hear from you what it does mean.

*The President:* (Smiles) Now he's put the responsibility on me to explain what he thought. So that's like asking Joseph to interpret your dream. Or Daniel to interpret your dream. That's very interesting.

*EXHORTATION*
You know, words are very important. How we construct what we say, especially if you're going to put it in a song that could be sung always by so many, it needs to be clear. It's very easy to assume. Anybody can assume what it means, but what does it really mean?
So why do we say "The Holyspirit is the beauty of my life?" If there's no beauty in your life, you can't claim it. It's just like some sinners, when you're preaching to them, who say "God is in all of us." It's not true. Some have Satan in them. And Jesus said it, "You are of your father, the devil. And the works of your Father, you will do." So we can't allow them to rub that on us.

Does something have glory because it exists? Satan exists. Does he have any glory? The reason you can say that the Holyspirit is the glory of your life is not because he's the glory of all life, because not all who live have glory. Some live unto themselves. There's no glory.
So, when I questioned it, I wanted to know what you meant. Do you mean that there's glory because you exist?
Before you were born again, you existed. When we talk about our life in Christ, it's a new life, not a new existence. When you're born again, you have a new life, "as if" you never existed before. "As if" because all things become new. But your body is the same, it doesn't become 2 months old like a baby's. No. It's spiritual. There's an existence. You become a new creature, as if you never existed before. You have a completely new life. But there is a history, so you became born again. The reason there is "again" is because there was a body.
We can't confuse the words of Jesus and say when you're born again, you never existed before. No. You're a new person. In the spirit, you are a new person. You have a new life that never existed before.
It's like bringing a new engine to replace an old one in a car. So you drop the first one, put in a new engine, but it's the same car. Now it's got a new engine, it's going to drive like a new engine, sound like a new engine... but it has a history. But that history doesn't concern the engine. That engine is brand new. And one day, that engine is going to get out of this body and go to heaven. For some, the body will change because the original body can't go there, it must undergo a transformation.

So, the question of existence beomes a conundrum. That's why I'm raising it. And you know, when you preach the Gospel, existence is a major debate on the matters of salvation. "What is existence?" I've been involved in some of such debates, and we're debating people who are into science, and sometimes certain occultic backgrounds. And the whole matter drags into awareness and reality. So now we're discussing existence, awareness, and reality.
So they ask a question, "What if we discovered we never existed... it was all a dream... we were all players in someone's dream? How can you prove we really exist?" So here's where we start discussing awareness. What is awareness?
When you're in a dream, you think you are doing what you're doing, saying what you're saying, meeting all the people you're meeting. Then you wake up and discover it was all a dream, and all the awareness you had never existed. So we move from there into debating reality. So what is reality?

*CONCLUSION*
That's why your terminologies are very important, so that it's not only what you mean by it, but what can be explanied.
"The glory of my existence." Is there glory because i exist?
Well, "The glory of my life," because I have a new life that's glorified in Christ. Do you get it?
So, generic communication, while acceptable, you also try to be careful in the play and use of words, because of the misunderstandings that cluld arise from there.
So if you don't want the debate, you might want to consider tweaking it to give what you want to say.

*Vashaun:* Sir, while you were explaining, something came to mind. I thought to run it by you, if it works. "The glory of the new creation."

*The President:* That would be an additional syllable.
Now that's a completely new direction, right?

*Dcn. A4:* The glory of my birth in Christ.

*The President:* Did you say "birth?" Like Simeon's "seed of his birth" today? (Smiles at the laughter) No, I just want to know. I just want to be sure.

*Dcn. A4:* Yes, Sir.

*The President:* Sing it, let me hear you.

(Laughs)
It sounds nice too. But I think several people can help us out there.
Ogey.
Ghana.
Yeah, alternative versions.
Saki.

But did you all understand what I said?

*Chisom:* Sir, "The glory of my life."

*The President:* Oh, it's in the second line? Life...

*DSA:* The glory of my destiny. The reason I said "destiny," Sir, when he said the "existence" thing, what I thought he was trying to say was our calling and destiny in Christ. That's why I said it, Sir.
I'm trying to replace it with "reality" Sir. I don't know if it's acceptable, Sir.

*The President:* (Laughs) Thank you.

*Ritasoul:* Sir, what about "My glorious and loving Father?"

*The President:* So, she's saying, let's get rid of the existential problem within the word "existence." (Smiles). I might agree with you.

*Ogey:* Thank you, Sir. Just that you have agreed with her.

*The President:* I said I might.

*Ogey:* Okay, Sir. If we're trying to replace that word, "The glory of my living."

*The President:* Actually, it describes what he was saying.
Sing it.

That was nice, really.

*Peter Bishut:* "The glory and beauty of my life/You are the joy and light of my life."

Okay. Sing it again.

Let me just take a look at the lyrics of this song.

*Thursday, 21st May 2026*

Faith Ejura.
You notice I didn't mention the title, right? I just called your name, for obvious reasons (smiles). Or, not very obvious reasons. I should say coded reasons.

(Chuckles) It was going well. And then when she modulated, I don't know what happened. It looked like everyone was singing a different song.
What happened there? Like everything scattered.

Peeyuu says they were praying for you (Ejura). That's quite interesting.
But I thought she did it well. Is it something you can repeat? Or did it just happen?
Oh, she has mastered it. Oh, wonderful!
Okay, so can you all stop praying for her and do your singing?

So, can we go from the bridge again?
Maybe I should first understand that coda. Can you sing that? So I'll know what it's supposed to be.

I would say, don't go into this part immediately after her modulation. It would seem like something went wrong.
So, from here, when she goes into "humanity," go to a proper landing with everyone, with "Now you reign through me." Then from there, go to this part.

Okay, the arrangement is better. But I want you to practice this coda, make it better. It's not coming out very nicely.
Did I hear something like "The great e-e-exchange?" What in the world was that?

Okay, so you're going to review that?

Thank you!

*Sunday, 17th May 2026*
*THE INSTRUCTION*
- The quality of the singing to be raised



*COMMENDATION*
The KING OF ETERNITY that you did at the stadium (during JTFC), it was amazing! It was amazing ! Wow! Still talking about it,
Thank you!

*DIALOGUE THAT LED TO THE INSTRUCTION*
I'm trying to understand this song.
Let me start from the smallest issues.

First, I would say, why did you bring in the line "All-conquering King?" It's not something that you would normally find. It's not a regular construction. It's constructed for another song, and it's even the title of that song. I don't know why it's here. It seems chipped in.

What do you mean when you say "Heaven sings, all creation bows?" When does heaven sing, and when does creation bow?

*Sylvia:* Sir, its a metaphor. Heaven rejoices, and all creation bows because he is.

*The President:* I don't get it. It simply means that heaven sings and creation bows. Because heaven does sing too, and creation bows too. It's written in the Bible. When you bring it in, it means that it's happening pari passu. But it's not.

Then, you said that the lion became the lamb. May I understand that? When did the lion become the lamb? How did that happen?

*Sylvia:* The "became the lamb" was an expression for when he died for the whole world.

*The President:* Yeah, but you're suggesting that he was a lion, and then he became a lamb. So at what point was he a lion, and when was the conversion? I'm just trying to understand it.

*Sylvia:* Thank you, Sir. Now that you've mentioned it, I see it.
Sir, I think that what Lyna Green was trying to explain on that line was that he is his personality. He is the lion of the tribe of Judah. Yet he was slain...


*The President:* That's my question. At what point did he become a lamb, and when was he a lion?

*Sylvia:* i would think, on the cross. When he was crucified.

*The President:* When was he a Lion?

*Sylvia:* From my understanding, Sir, he was foretold to be the King of Israel, born a king. One of his titles is the lion of the tribe of Judah, Sir. This is who he was foretold to be. He came as the Lion of the tribe of Judah, and still became the Lamb that was slain for all. That's the truth that we were trying to communicate with the line, Sir.


*EXHORTATION*
*The President:* In Revelation 5:4-8
The place you're referring to is here. In fact, there are two lines in the song that are lifted from the 5th verse. So, the says "The lion of the tribe of Judah hath prevailed."
My question was, when was he a lion, and when was he the lamb? Because the song says "The lion who became the lamb..." So, did the lion become the lamb? ... is my question.

You have to follow prophetic revelation. He's telling John of one who prevailed. He prevailed not as a lamb. So he says "The lion of the tribe of Judah hath prevailed,." Meaning that here, in his victory, he is called a lion. Not that he was previously a lion and became a lamb, but that in his victory, he is identified as the lion that came from the tribe of Judah.

And then he called him the root of David, signifying that he preexisted the time. And to show him who he was referring to, verse 6 says, "And I beheld, and lo, in the midst of the throne and of the four beasts, and in the midst of the elders, stood a Lamb that had been slain."

The KJV rendering here is a bit awkward, but it shows that some words are missing, so they put it in parentheses. But if I read it to you from the CJB, it says "in the circle of the elders, a Lamb that appeared to have been slaughtered..."

The NIV says "then i saw a Lamb looking as if it had been slain." This is supposed to be a lamb that's dead. It looks killed.
Then verse 7 says, "And he came and took the scroll out of the right hand of the one sitting on the throne." I thought he was dead? Did you no5tce? The Lamb looked dead/slaughtered.

Then suddenly, this seemingly dead lamb got up and took the book out of the hand of the one who sat on the throne. Then in verse 8, when he had taken the scroll, the four beasts and 24 elders fell on the ground, and they all began to worship the Lamb. That's wonderful!

Remember, the book of Revelation is full of symbolisms. Remember that he wasn't slain again. So this is referring to the One who was slain on the cross. And the fact that he was seeing a vision: the lamb who looks killed, looks like a dead man. But now the dead man is qualified to open the book. So there was a resurrection of the Lamb that was slain. Right? So we see that resurrection in this place.
So you can see how, in prophetic revelation, he looks at the past and tells us of the present as it were. In that present, he was crying cause nobody could open the book. So the angel says "Don't cry. See, the Lion of the tribe of Judah has prevailed." He asks who is it. The they showed him the lamb that was dead, but gets up, and appears to open the book. And everyone is worshipping him. It's all symbolism.
So, we will not say that the Lion became the Lamb. The song already says that the Lion and the Lamb is alive today. It doesn't necessarily wave from one to the other. These are his titles. He holds the titles. He holds the title of the Lion because he's victorious. So it would have even made more sense if the Lamb became the Lion, because he won the victory when he opened the book. Because he was qualified to open the book, he is called the Lion of the tribe of Judah. It says "hath prevailed" to open the book. Where is he? And they show us the Lamb.

*CONCLUSION*
Asides those things you're to fix lyrically, is there anything you'd like to do to this song to make it a great song?
Good song, but it's just there. Which means that we can decide to leave it there, so when we're looking for songs, we add it.
Or, you raise the quality of the song.

Okay, so raise the quality of the song.

Thank you!

*Monday, 21st July 2026*


That was very beautiful!

Thank you very much!

What I want us to do later is to get a duet, with a lady and a guy leading it.
Now, I know several of you know it and lead it in your churches, so we may not have the time to go through everyone.

Marleea, you know the song, right?
Good!

Voice texture matters.
Timing matters, with respect to the required rhythm of the song. Now, that can be affected by your internal rhythm. You know you have a rhythm. Now that rhythm controls all your songs. So you're more consistent with that rhythm. That's why sometimes, a lead singer may not be the best for a particular song. That's also why sometimes, you find you're either lagging behind, or you're in front. That can be easily cured for some people. (Smiles) Now I say cured like it's a problem. That can become a problem if you fall out of line. More practice and singing can help to dissolve that.
It's like in a game where all members have to do well if they practice as a team. So you rehearse and sing properly with them.

Thank you!

comments.text:
*Sunday, 19th July 2026*

*THE INSTRUCTION*
*- "The Lord already made you whole" in the bridge was changed to "You will be healed in Jesus name."*
*- "Devils" to be replaced with "demons" in the chorus.*

*THE DIALOGUE THAT LED TO INSTRUCTION*
Thank you very much!

Just a couple of things.
The first one, I didn't really like the way you pronounced the "centurion." In your singing, it sounded like a completely different word. Because of the way you said0g, it can be assumed that it's a completely different word.

Then, in the pre-chorus, I would rather use the word "demons" for "devils." You've got it in two lines there in the chorus. So, replace the word "devils" with "demons" in the chorus.
And by the way, in the verse, you noticed you already used the word "demons" already. So that just goes with what I was saying.

The other one. I've got a bit of a question. It opens the bridge by saying, "The Lord already made you whole." If the Lord already made you whole, why is the moment coming? Cause it says, "The moment is here for your miracle," and then "The Lord already made you whole."
It says, "We declare to you that you'll be healed." So why the inconsistency?

*Pst. Sylvia:* Thank you, Sir. That line where we have "You'll be healed," what I had there before was "We declare to you his finished works." So when I changed that, it didn't seem correct.

*The President:* Yeah. It's a healing program, so it's incorrect. What I would rather change here is "The Lord already made you whole." It challenges everything else you're saying.

*Pst. Sylvia:* Alright, Sir. I'll change that, Sir. I'll put it in the present continuous like what we have in the song.

*The President:* Let me explain something to you. And it will help you in considering your lyrical content.
It is true that Jesus Christ completed everything for salvation. So legally, all the world is saved. Right? Because God's not holding their sins against them, for the very fact that Jesus paid the full penalty for sin. But then, why did Peter tell the whole house of Israel that they shall be saved if they believed in Jesus? Why did Paul tell the jailer, "Believe in the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shall be Saved?" And in Romans 10:9 "If you will confess with your mouth the Lord Jesus, and shall believe that God raised him from the dead, thou shall be saved?" But they're all saved, legally. But they haven't entered into vital salvation.
So, wholeness is a completely different thing, except that the word "saved" is an all-inclusive word which, on one hand, is beautiful because it includes everything. On the other hand, it makes your analysis of salvation a little bit more clumsy, except you know the details of the scripture. So that's why it can be like a contradiction for some, while it is perfectly in order.
So when you're dealing with sinners, you have to have a consistency in your delivery.
For example, every sinner is saved legally. But not a one of those sinners is righteous before God. Can you see it? Because to be righteous, you must believe in Jesus Christ. You must believe. You must believe in his resurrection. You must believe. You must. If you don't believe, you cannot have his righteousness. But that righteousness was consummated in Christ 2,000 years ago, and legally made available to all men. But you cannot be righteous until you believe.
Do you get it?
Yeah. So that's the same thing as being made whole. The wholeness, you will not enter until you believe. And that's what your song is saying here. "Just say 'Yes, I believe it.'"
And that's why I said it can become clumsy when we mix them up.
Like in the Healing Streams, we say "God will heal you," because God is doing it anyway. And I've explained before, it's not like God is doing some work about it. We're bringing them healing through the Gospel of Jesus. What he already did in Christ. The salvation that we are now covers everything. But we have to be consistent in the presentation.
"Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shall be saved." That's God's word.
So, we separate the legal from the vital.

So that's the line I think you should change. The one in the bridge.

*Pst. Sylvia:* Pastor Sir, what about "You will be healed In Jesus name?"

*The President:* Yeah.

*Pst. Sylvia:* Thank you, Sir.

Thank you!

*Sunday, 19th July 2026*

*THE INSTRUCTION*
*- "The Lord already made you whole" in the bridge was changed to "You will be healed in Jesus name."*
*- "Devils" to be replaced with "demons" in the chorus.*

*THE DIALOGUE THAT LED TO INSTRUCTION*
Thank you very much!

Just a couple of things.
The first one, I didn't really like the way you pronounced the "centurion." In your singing, it sounded like a completely different word. Because of the way you said0g, it can be assumed that it's a completely different word.

Then, in the pre-chorus, I would rather use the word "demons" for "devils." You've got it in two lines there in the chorus. So, replace the word "devils" with "demons" in the chorus.
And by the way, in the verse, you noticed you already used the word "demons" already. So that just goes with what I was saying.

The other one. I've got a bit of a question. It opens the bridge by saying, "The Lord already made you whole." If the Lord already made you whole, why is the moment coming? Cause it says, "The moment is here for your miracle," and then "The Lord already made you whole."
It says, "We declare to you that you'll be healed." So why the inconsistency?

*Pst. Sylvia:* Thank you, Sir. That line where we have "You'll be healed," what I had there before was "We declare to you his finished works." So when I changed that, it didn't seem correct.

*The President:* Yeah. It's a healing program, so it's incorrect. What I would rather change here is "The Lord already made you whole." It challenges everything else you're saying.

*Pst. Sylvia:* Alright, Sir. I'll change that, Sir. I'll put it in the present continuous like what we have in the song.

*The President:* Let me explain something to you. And it will help you in considering your lyrical content.
It is true that Jesus Christ completed everything for salvation. So legally, all the world is saved. Right? Because God's not holding their sins against them, for the very fact that Jesus paid the full penalty for sin. But then, why did Peter tell the whole house of Israel that they shall be saved if they believed in Jesus? Why did Paul tell the jailer, "Believe in the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shall be Saved?" And in Romans 10:9 "If you will confess with your mouth the Lord Jesus, and shall believe that God raised him from the dead, thou shall be saved?" But they're all saved, legally. But they haven't entered into vital salvation.
So, wholeness is a completely different thing, except that the word "saved" is an all-inclusive word which, on one hand, is beautiful because it includes everything. On the other hand, it makes your analysis of salvation a little bit more clumsy, except you know the details of the scripture. So that's why it can be like a contradiction for some, while it is perfectly in order.
So when you're dealing with sinners, you have to have a consistency in your delivery.
For example, every sinner is saved legally. But not a one of those sinners is righteous before God. Can you see it? Because to be righteous, you must believe in Jesus Christ. You must believe. You must believe in his resurrection. You must believe. You must. If you don't believe, you cannot have his righteousness. But that righteousness was consummated in Christ 2,000 years ago, and legally made available to all men. But you cannot be righteous until you believe.
Do you get it?
Yeah. So that's the same thing as being made whole. The wholeness, you will not enter until you believe. And that's what your song is saying here. "Just say 'Yes, I believe it.'"
And that's why I said it can become clumsy when we mix them up.
Like in the Healing Streams, we say "God will heal you," because God is doing it anyway. And I've explained before, it's not like God is doing some work about it. We're bringing them healing through the Gospel of Jesus. What he already did in Christ. The salvation that we are now covers everything. But we have to be consistent in the presentation.
"Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shall be saved." That's God's word.
So, we separate the legal from the vital.

So that's the line I think you should change. The one in the bridge.

*Pst. Sylvia:* Pastor Sir, what about "You will be healed In Jesus name?"

*The President:* Yeah.

*Pst. Sylvia:* Thank you, Sir.

Thank you!

So, this song is done as simple as possible, not to get in trouble.

*Sammie:* The verse.

That part turns you on?

*The President:* Then, the chorus. "Lord Jesus, you are/The beginning and the end/Faithful and true/None compares to you/Source of truth/The everlasting God/King of the earth/All power is yours."
Wow! Wonderful!
(The President sings) "Source of truth/The everlasting God/King of the earth/All power is yours." Right? Did I get that part?

*Sammie:* Very well, Sir.

*The President:* I got it? How could I? Okay. So, it's very simple.
You really want us to sing this song in the coming Praise Service?

*Sammie:* I would love to, Sir.

*The President:* I don't mean whether you would love to. I mean, you want us to sing it?

*Sammie:* Whatever you want us to do, Sir.

*The President:* What I want us to do? I didn't invite you before you brought it up here.
And I noticed you were also trying to stay away from the previous way. You just made it softer.

So, I want us to put you through some more complex songs. Get him to sing some more complex songs, just to free him from the monotony. I mean, he's a good singer, no doubt. We need to get him to do some other songs.

There are some of you, I notice when you sing other songs in church, and you sing well. But when you come here, it's like you're restricted to some particular songs.

I think we should put Sammie on overdrive. He would love it!

*Ogey:* Pastor Sir, if you would permit me, I wanted to suggest HEAVENLY FATHER by Pst. Saki.

*The President:* I agree. I mean, he will try it. Yeah. Why not?
Thank you. Good one!

*Evang:* Pastor, good evening, Sir. I don't know if it's the same issue that's happening with Sis. Rozey.
Pastor, you once gave an experiment many years ago. You said you put an insect in a bottle and capped it. The insect jumped and jumped, trying to come out, but couldn't. When the cap was removed, it still couldn't get up there, because it had been conditioned.
Now, surely, the issue that Sis. Rozey had, and which several other people also had... When the great exchange happened, it was like she was going to faint, so we had to do something. But Dcn. Isaiah and Dcn. Kelly were not in agreement.

Pastor Sir, I'm saying this so that you can help us. The fear of failing, the fear not being accepted, and the fear of not getting that standard that you've set for us, if these can be taken care of, Rozey can become the best singer on earth.

This is what we've been dealing with actually. It was to save a soul. So I told her to remain there, and when Pastor asks, I will explain. This is really the issue. If Rozey would do a thousand rehearsals and not take care of this, it's a problem.
If Sammie is having that kind of mind also, there's an issue.
Pastor Sir, you've given us wings to fly. Sir, if you can help us, this great exchange will work for her, and bring out the best results.

*The President:* (Smiles) So Rozey, you were crying because I said you should move from Soprano to Alto? I told you yesterday that that was not a demotion. It's the flesh. Imagine if you think you're a great singer, and you're put in a place where those people are not as good, then there's a mistake.

I think recently, probably in the last few weeks, probably Michaela has done more songs than most, except Maya maybe. Where's she singing from? Alto.
Think how many songs Rita has done. Or Eniola. They've done more songs than most people on this side (Soprano). So don't feel bad about those things. And when I tell you to do something, even if you don't understand it at that time, know that it's for your best interests. Look at it from both sides, for ministry and for you as a person. If it's good for the ministry but not good for you, I'm not going to do it. If it's good for you but not good for the ministry, I'm not going to do it. I always like to ensure that it's good for both.

It's the same thing like when we want to transfer a pastor. I want to make sure that pastor should be in that place. If you make someone do something that God does not sanction, you'll bear responsibility. It's a displacement, because you're helping someone to stay outside of God's work. It doesn't matter whether he succeeds or fails. That's not important. What's important is, is he in the centre of God's will? Why would you make someone do something that God does not accept? Why would you help a man/woman to get out of God's will? Who wants to bear such a responsibility? At least not me.

In the last couple of days before you came here, Friday into Saturday, I was speaking to a studio audience of the Global Ministers' Classroom. One of the things I said to them was that I like to see what I'm going to do before I do it. And that's the way I've done most things, cause I believe very much in visions. Not dreams. I don't take dreams seriously. I believe in visions. So I like to know what a person should do before I encourage a person to do it. I don't like guess work. And I haven't misled a single person yet.
So, what you just need is some confidence. The Praise Night that we are doing, do we say Praise Night with Rozey? No. With Pastor Chris. So if that same Pastor Chris is saying "sit on this side," be happy. Don't feel bad. We love you very much! Don't feel bad. At least I do. Yes! Don't be sad.

So, always have confidence, alright? The direction that we give is always in your interest. Always. We may talk to a few of you more than others, but it doesn't mean that they are priced more than you. But we have to talk with a few that help give inspiration/help/direction to others. I may not meet with everybody here individually. But at least, with a few, it sends a message.
I think it was some weeks ago when we were here, I asked if some people knew the song. The ones who didn't, I said 500 Espees each. Where are they? Did you get it? Oh, but you didn't acknowledge. You were going to do that today? Where have you been all this while? How much is 500 Espees? Almost a million Naira. How can someone give you almost a million Naira and you don't even acknowledge that they did? No, no, no, no, I'm not saying that they're not grateful. They are very grateful, I can see that. And I've not been here, really. But that's the point. Even though they're grateful they received a gift, they don't even have the chance to walk their way to meet me.
Okay, Eli-J wants to see me, he goes to stop me when I'm getting into the vehicle. You get it? So he gets to see me. That doesn't mean that I don't love those ones there, but some people do get an opportunity ahead of others. Right?

Thank you!

So, I've received your acknowledgement from your standing (500 Espees beneficiaries). I'm glad you got it.

*Sunday, 19th July 2026*

*THE INSTRUCTION*
*- "The Lord already made you whole" in the bridge was changed to "You will be healed in Jesus name."*
*- "Devils" to be replaced with "demons" in the chorus.*

*THE DIALOGUE THAT LED TO INSTRUCTION*
Thank you very much!

Just a couple of things.
The first one, I didn't really like the way you pronounced the "centurion." In your singing, it sounded like a completely different word. Because of the way you said0g, it can be assumed that it's a completely different word.

Then, in the pre-chorus, I would rather use the word "demons" for "devils." You've got it in two lines there in the chorus. So, replace the word "devils" with "demons" in the chorus.
And by the way, in the verse, you noticed you already used the word "demons" already. So that just goes with what I was saying.

The other one. I've got a bit of a question. It opens the bridge by saying, "The Lord already made you whole." If the Lord already made you whole, why is the moment coming? Cause it says, "The moment is here for your miracle," and then "The Lord already made you whole."
It says, "We declare to you that you'll be healed." So why the inconsistency?

*Pst. Sylvia:* Thank you, Sir. That line where we have "You'll be healed," what I had there before was "We declare to you his finished works." So when I changed that, it didn't seem correct.

*The President:* Yeah. It's a healing program, so it's incorrect. What I would rather change here is "The Lord already made you whole." It challenges everything else you're saying.

*Pst. Sylvia:* Alright, Sir. I'll change that, Sir. I'll put it in the present continuous like what we have in the song.

*The President:* Let me explain something to you. And it will help you in considering your lyrical content.
It is true that Jesus Christ completed everything for salvation. So legally, all the world is saved. Right? Because God's not holding their sins against them, for the very fact that Jesus paid the full penalty for sin. But then, why did Peter tell the whole house of Israel that they shall be saved if they believed in Jesus? Why did Paul tell the jailer, "Believe in the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shall be Saved?" And in Romans 10:9 "If you will confess with your mouth the Lord Jesus, and shall believe that God raised him from the dead, thou shall be saved?" But they're all saved, legally. But they haven't entered into vital salvation.
So, wholeness is a completely different thing, except that the word "saved" is an all-inclusive word which, on one hand, is beautiful because it includes everything. On the other hand, it makes your analysis of salvation a little bit more clumsy, except you know the details of the scripture. So that's why it can be like a contradiction for some, while it is perfectly in order.
So when you're dealing with sinners, you have to have a consistency in your delivery.
For example, every sinner is saved legally. But not a one of those sinners is righteous before God. Can you see it? Because to be righteous, you must believe in Jesus Christ. You must believe. You must believe in his resurrection. You must believe. You must. If you don't believe, you cannot have his righteousness. But that righteousness was consummated in Christ 2,000 years ago, and legally made available to all men. But you cannot be righteous until you believe.
Do you get it?
Yeah. So that's the same thing as being made whole. The wholeness, you will not enter until you believe. And that's what your song is saying here. "Just say 'Yes, I believe it.'"
And that's why I said it can become clumsy when we mix them up.
Like in the Healing Streams, we say "God will heal you," because God is doing it anyway. And I've explained before, it's not like God is doing some work about it. We're bringing them healing through the Gospel of Jesus. What he already did in Christ. The salvation that we are now covers everything. But we have to be consistent in the presentation.
"Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shall be saved." That's God's word.
So, we separate the legal from the vital.

So that's the line I think you should change. The one in the bridge.

*Pst. Sylvia:* Pastor Sir, what about "You will be healed In Jesus name?"

*The President:* Yeah.

*Pst. Sylvia:* Thank you, Sir.

Thank you!
